questions.question: Who among the following composer gained global recognition for his song 'Naatu Naatu' from action film RRR?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**MM Keeravani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MM Keeravani** is a renowned Indian music composer, playback singer, and lyricist.
 
• He gained global recognition for his song **'Naatu Naatu'**, featured in the action film **RRR**.
 
• The song **'Naatu Naatu'** won the **Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song** in 2023, making it the first Indian song to win this prestigious accolade.
 
• **MM Keeravani** has primarily worked in the **Telugu cinema** industry, but his compositions have also been featured in other Indian languages such as Hindi, Tamil, and Kannada.
 
• He has collaborated extensively with **SS Rajamouli**, the director of RRR, on several blockbuster films.
 
• MM Keeravani is celebrated for his ability to blend **Indian classical music** with contemporary styles, creating memorable soundtracks that resonate with audiences worldwide.
 
• Besides 'Naatu Naatu,' his other notable works include compositions for films like **Baahubali**, **Annamayya**, **Pelli Sandadi**, and **Eega**.
 
• MM Keeravani's contribution to Indian cinema has earned him numerous awards, including **National Film Awards, Filmfare Awards, and State Nandi Awards.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **AR Rahman**__

 __
 
• **AR Rahman** is one of India's most celebrated music composers, known for his versatility and innovation in music.
 
• He won two **Academy Awards (Oscars)** for his work in the film **Slumdog Millionaire** (Best Original Score and Best Original Song - "Jai Ho").
 
• Rahman has composed music for numerous acclaimed films, such as **Roja**, **Bombay**, **Lagaan**, and **127 Hours**.
 
• He is often referred to as the **Mozart of Madras** and has been honored with several **Grammy Awards, BAFTA Awards, and National Film Awards.**
 
 
 
• **KJ Yesudas**__
 __
 
• **KJ Yesudas** is an iconic playback singer from India, primarily known for his contributions to Indian classical and film music.
 
• He has sung in multiple Indian languages, including **Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada, Bengali, and Sanskrit.**
 
• Yesudas is a recipient of several prestigious awards, such as the **Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.**
 
• While he is a celebrated singer, he is not known for composing music like MM Keeravani.
 
 
 
• **SP Balasubramanium**__
 
 
• **SP Balasubramanium**, often referred to as **SPB**, was a legendary playback singer, music director, and actor.
 
• He sang over **40,000 songs** in multiple Indian languages, including Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Hindi, and Malayalam.
 
• SPB won numerous accolades, including **National Film Awards, Filmfare Awards, and State Nandi Awards.**
 
• Though he contributed immensely to Indian music, he was primarily recognized as a singer rather than a composer like MM Keeravani.

questions.question: Uzhavar Thirunal is a farmers festival celebrated in which state?
questions.solution:

• **Uzhavar Thirunal**, also known as Farmers’ Festival, is celebrated in the state of **Tamil Nadu**.

• It is a time dedicated to honoring and expressing gratitude to farmers for their contributions to agriculture and the economy.
 
• During this festival, people acknowledge the importance of agriculture, which is the backbone of **Tamil Nadu's economy**.
 
• **Traditional dishes** are prepared using fresh harvest produce, and communities come together to celebrate.
 
• Farmers offer prayers to the Sun God and other deities for a prosperous agricultural season.
 
• The festival also highlights **cultural performances, traditional games, and exhibitions**, showcasing Tamil Nadu's rich heritage.
 
• Uzhavar Thirunal reflects the significance of agriculture in Tamil Nadu and promotes the idea of sustainability and respect for nature.

 __
 
• Kerala is known for its harvest festival called **Onam**, which is celebrated with great enthusiasm across the state.
 
• **Onam** marks the homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali and includes rituals, feasts, boat races, and traditional dances.
 
• Kerala is often referred to as **"God's Own Country"** due to its scenic beauty and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__

• It involves rituals, traditional food, and kite flying to mark the harvest season.
 
• Sankranti is also associated with the worship of cattle, which play a significant role in agriculture.

questions.question: In archery, what is the highest score for hitting the inner gold ring with a single arrow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **archery**, the scoring system is based on the part of the target an arrow hits.
 
• The **target face** consists of concentric rings, with the innermost ring known as the **inner gold ring**.
 
• The **inner gold ring** represents the highest scoring area, and hitting this ring with an arrow gives a maximum score of **10 points.**
 
• This scoring system is standard in most archery formats, including **Olympic archery** and other international competitions.
 
• A **perfect score** in a round of archery depends on the number of arrows shot, but hitting the **inner gold ring** consistently is the key to achieving the highest possible score.
 
• Accurate aim, proper technique, and focus are critical for archers to hit this high-value target zone.
 
• This scoring system ensures fairness and rewards precision, making archery a highly competitive and skill-oriented sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Concepts in Archery Scoring**__

 __
 
• The **target face** in archery is divided into several colored rings, each representing a specific score value ranging from **1 to 10**.
 
• The **gold rings** are located at the center of the target and are worth the highest points, with the **outer gold ring** scoring **9 points** and the **inner gold ring** scoring **10 points.**
 
• Archery competitions can be held in various formats, including **indoor, outdoor, and field archery**, each with specific rules and target distances.
 
• In some formats, a perfect score can result from hitting the **inner gold ring** multiple times in a round.
 
 
 
• **Importance of 10-Point Scoring**__
 
 
• The **10-point score** is a benchmark for excellence in archery and is often targeted by professional and competitive archers.
 
• It also requires a combination of skills such as **precision, steadiness, and mental focus**, making it a challenging yet rewarding achievement.
 
• In major tournaments like the **Olympics**, archers aim for the inner gold ring to secure victory and achieve high rankings.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution safeguards the freedom of religion in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 25** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the **freedom of religion** to every individual.
 
• This article provides all persons with the right to freely **profess, practice, and propagate their religion**, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• It ensures that individuals can follow their religious beliefs without interference, as long as they do not violate laws or disrupt public harmony.
 
• It applies to **citizens and non-citizens** alike, making it a universal right for all individuals residing in India.
 
• However, the article allows the state to regulate or restrict activities related to religion in the interest of **social welfare and reform**, such as the abolition of practices like untouchability.
 
• **Freedom of religion** is one of the fundamental rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article plays a crucial role in ensuring **secularism**, which is a key feature of India's democratic framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 27**__

 __
 
• **Article 27** prohibits individuals from being compelled to pay any taxes that are specifically allocated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.
 
• This article ensures that the state does not favor any religion financially and maintains a **secular approach** in its operations.
 
 
 
• **Article 28**__
 __
 
• **Article 28** deals with the freedom from attending religious instruction or religious worship in educational institutions wholly maintained by the state.
 
• It ensures that no individual is forced to participate in religious activities in such institutions, safeguarding the principle of **secular education**.
 
 
 
• **Article 26**__
 
 
• **Article 26** grants every religious denomination or its sections the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
 
• It also allows them to manage their own affairs in matters of religion, own and acquire property, and administer it in accordance with the law.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the density of the population of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**382 persons/km²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Census of India 2011** is the 15th National Census conducted by the Government of India.
 
• The **population density** is defined as the number of people living per unit area (per square kilometer).
 
• As per the Census of India 2011, the **population density of India** was recorded as **382 persons/km².**
 
• This marked an increase from the previous census (2001), which reported a density of **325 persons/km².**
 
• Higher population density indicates a more concentrated population in certain areas, especially in states like **Bihar, West Bengal, and Kerala.**
 
• The states with the highest population density in 2011 were **Bihar (1106 persons/km²)** and **West Bengal (1028 persons/km²).**
 
• India's population density is influenced by factors like availability of resources, geographical conditions, and urbanization.
 
• Regions with lower population density include mountainous and desert areas, such as **Arunachal Pradesh (17 persons/km²)** and **Rajasthan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Census of India 2011**__

 __
 
• The Census of India 2011 was conducted under the supervision of the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.**
 
• It recorded a total population of **1.21 billion.**
 
• The literacy rate of India in 2011 was recorded at **74.04%.**
 
• It also provided insights into other factors such as **sex ratio, urbanization trends, and household amenities.**
 
 
 
• **Population Density Trends**__
 
 
• States like **Bihar** and **West Bengal** have consistently reported high population density due to better agricultural resources and urban concentration.
 
• Regions like the **Northeast** and parts of **Rajasthan** have lower density due to geographical constraints like mountains and deserts.
 
• Population density serves as an important metric for planning and resource allocation.

questions.question: What were the main objectives of the Rolling Plan introduced between the Fifth and Sixth Five-Year Plans?

options.text: Focus on economic crisis management and policy adjustments
Growth with social justice and economic stability

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Focus on economic crisis management and policy adjustments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rolling Plan** was introduced in **1978** by the **Janata Party government** led by **Prime Minister Morarji Desai**.
 
• The primary objective of the Rolling Plan was to address the **economic instability** caused by the **global oil crisis of the 1970s** and the subsequent **domestic economic issues**.
 
• The plan focused on **policy adjustments** to stabilize the economy and manage the **crisis effectively**.
 
• Unlike the fixed Five-Year Plans, the Rolling Plan was **flexible** and allowed for **annual revisions** based on the prevailing economic conditions.
 
• It aimed to provide a **short-term response** to economic challenges while maintaining a **medium-term perspective** on growth and development.
 
• The plan emphasized the need for **fiscal discipline**, **reduction of inflation**, and a balanced approach to **resource allocation**.
 
• It was a significant departure from the traditional planning process, allowing for **greater adaptability** in economic policy-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Employment generation and regional balance**__

 __
 
• This objective was central to the **Second Five-Year Plan**, which focused on **industrialization** and ensuring **balanced regional development**.
 
• It aimed to reduce disparities in regional development by creating **employment opportunities** in less developed areas.
 
 
 
• **Growth with social justice and economic stability**__
 __
 
• This was the focus of the **Fourth Five-Year Plan**, which emphasized **inclusive growth** and **poverty alleviation**.
 
• The plan sought to combine economic growth with **social justice**, ensuring that the benefits of development reached all sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural expansion and industrial growth**__
 
 
• This was the main objective of the **Third Five-Year Plan**, which aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in **food grain production** and promote **industrialization**.
 
• The focus was on **agriculture and industry** as the twin pillars of economic development.

questions.question: How many inscriptions make up the Edicts of Ashoka?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Edicts of Ashoka** are a collection of **33 inscriptions** engraved on **pillars, boulders, and cave walls**, created during the reign of the Mauryan emperor **Ashoka** (c. 268–232 BCE).
 
• These inscriptions are found across the Indian subcontinent, including regions in modern-day **India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Afghanistan**.
 
• The edicts are written in several languages, including **Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic**, and are inscribed in various scripts, such as the **Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts**.
 
• The main purpose of these edicts was to propagate Ashoka’s policy of **Dhamma** (a code of moral and ethical conduct).
 
• The edicts can be classified into several categories: **Pillar Edicts, Major Rock Edicts, and Minor Rock Edicts**.
 
• They highlight Ashoka’s efforts to promote **Buddhism**, his dedication to the welfare of his people, and his emphasis on nonviolence, tolerance, and compassion.
 
• The most famous of these inscriptions is the **Kalinga Edict**, which reflects Ashoka’s remorse after the destructive Kalinga War and his subsequent commitment to nonviolence.
 
• The inscriptions are an important source for understanding the **history, administration, and cultural practices** of the Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of the Edicts**__

 __
 
• The edicts provide insights into the **administrative policies** of the Mauryan Empire and Ashoka’s role as a ruler.
 
• They emphasize principles such as **religious tolerance, social welfare, and moral responsibility**.
 
• The inscriptions also demonstrate Ashoka’s adoption of **Buddhism** and his efforts to spread its teachings across his empire and beyond.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Edicts**__
 
 
• The inscriptions are unique for their use of multiple **languages and scripts**, reflecting the diversity of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• They serve as some of the earliest examples of written records in Indian history, contributing significantly to the study of **epigraphy and linguistics**.
 
• They are widely regarded as a testament to Ashoka’s progressive and humanitarian approach to governance.

questions.question: The Ganga delta and coastal plains of which state are affected by storms with heavy rains almost every third or fifth day in July and August?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ganga delta** and coastal plains of Odisha are frequently affected by **storms and heavy rains**, especially during the **monsoon season (July and August).**
 
• Odisha’s geographical location along the **Bay of Bengal** makes it particularly vulnerable to **cyclonic storms** and heavy rainfall.
 
• These storms are often associated with **low-pressure systems** that form over the Bay of Bengal and intensify, causing disruptions in the region.
 
• Such weather phenomena lead to **waterlogging, flooding, and agricultural losses** in the state.
 
• Odisha has experienced several **catastrophic cyclones**, such as the **1999 Super Cyclone**, which caused widespread devastation.
 
• The government of Odisha has implemented various **disaster management initiatives** to mitigate the impact of these storms, including the establishment of **cyclone shelters** and early warning systems.
 
• The coastal plains of Odisha also benefit from a fertile soil composition, which is vital for **agriculture**, but the recurring storms often disrupt farming activities.
 
• Odisha’s climatic conditions during July and August are largely influenced by the **Southwest Monsoon**, which brings heavy rainfall to the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__

 __
 
• Tamil Nadu is primarily affected by cyclonic storms during the **Northeast Monsoon season**, which occurs between **October and December**.
 
• It receives less rainfall from the **Southwest Monsoon** compared to other states on the eastern coast.
 
• The coastal areas of Tamil Nadu are vulnerable to storms originating in the **Bay of Bengal**, but these are less frequent during July and August.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 __
 
• Gujarat is located on the western coast of India and is primarily affected by cyclonic storms originating in the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• Monsoonal rainfall in Gujarat is significant but does not typically involve frequent storms like those in Odisha.
 
• The state faces occasional cyclones during the **post-monsoon season** or early monsoon period.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**__
 
 
• Maharashtra experiences monsoonal rainfall, particularly in the **Western Ghats** region, but it is not prone to frequent cyclonic storms during July and August.
 
• The state’s coastal areas, such as Mumbai and Konkan, are more affected by heavy rains due to the monsoon rather than storms.
 
• Unlike Odisha, Maharashtra’s geographical features do not make it highly vulnerable to cyclones from the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which dance and singing form of Manipur was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sankirtana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sankirtana** is a traditional dance and singing form of Manipur that was inscribed on the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** by UNESCO in **2013**.
 
• It is primarily performed by the **Vaishnava community** in Manipur, reflecting their **devotion to Lord Krishna.**
 
• The performance integrates **singing, drumming, and dancing** and is considered a sacred ritual in the Vaishnava tradition.
 
• **Pung (traditional drum)** and **Kartal (cymbals)** are the primary musical instruments used during Sankirtana performances.
 
• The dance form portrays **episodes from the life of Lord Krishna** and is performed during various religious and social ceremonies, such as weddings and celebrations.
 
• Sankirtana is not just an art form but also a tool for **community bonding**, as it fosters spiritual and social harmony among the people of Manipur.
 
• It is a vital part of the **Vaishnava culture** and reflects the rich cultural heritage and traditions of Manipur.
 
• UNESCO recognized Sankirtana for its **unique oral traditions**, its ability to preserve history and spirituality, and its role in strengthening community ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ras Lila**__

 __
 
• **Ras Lila** is another traditional dance form of Manipur that narrates the **divine love story of Lord Krishna and Radha.**
 
• It is performed in Manipuri temples during religious festivals and holds a significant place in the **Vaishnava culture.**
 
• However, Ras Lila has not been inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage like Sankirtana.
 
 
 
• **Maibi**__
 __
 
• **Maibi dance** is a ritualistic dance performed by the **Maibi priestesses** of Manipur.
 
• It is associated with the **Lai Haraoba festival**, which celebrates the creation stories of the Manipuri people.
 
• Maibi dance has cultural significance but is not on the UNESCO Representative List.
 
 
 
• **Cymbal**__
 
 
• **Cymbals** are musical instruments that are used in various traditional and religious performances in India, including Sankirtana.
 
• However, cymbals themselves are not a dance or singing form, but rather an **instrumental component** of many performances.

__
 
• **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)** is the statutory authority responsible for regulating civil aviation in India.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Civil Aviation** and ensures compliance with the **Aircraft Act, 1934** and the rules made thereunder.
 
• The DGCA is tasked with ensuring **safety standards** for aircraft operations, airworthiness, and crew licensing.
 
• The DGCA regulates aviation activities including **air traffic services, aerodrome standards, and passenger safety.**
 
• It oversees the implementation of **International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards** in India.
 
• The DGCA also investigates **aviation incidents and accidents** to enhance safety measures and prevent future occurrences.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in issuing **civil aviation directives, guidelines, and certifications** for operators and pilots.
 
• Established as a statutory body under the **Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024**, it strengthens regulatory mechanisms and ensures compliance with global aviation norms.
 
• The DGCA collaborates with international aviation authorities for **technical cooperation and exchange programs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)**__

 __
 
• The **Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau** is an independent agency under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
 
• It is responsible for investigating **aircraft accidents and incidents** in India to determine their causes and make recommendations to prevent future occurrences.
 
• The AAIB works in collaboration with the DGCA but does not regulate safety standards directly.
 
• Its role is limited to investigation and reporting, unlike the DGCA, which has a broader regulatory function.
 
 
 
• **Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS)**__
 __
 
• The **Bureau of Civil Aviation Security** (BCAS) is responsible for ensuring aviation security standards in India.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Civil Aviation** and focuses on preventing unlawful interference in civil aviation operations.
 
• The BCAS formulates guidelines for **security checks, screening procedures, and anti-terrorism measures** at airports.
 
• Unlike the DGCA, which regulates overall aviation safety, the BCAS specifically focuses on **security aspects**.
 
 
 
• **Aircraft Accidents Investigation Committee**__
 
 
• The **Aircraft Accidents Investigation Committee** is not a statutory body but rather an ad-hoc panel formed for specific investigations.
 
• It lacks the dedicated infrastructure and regulatory authority of the AAIB or DGCA.
 
• Such committees are usually formed for certain high-profile accidents or incidents to supplement the work of agencies like the AAIB.

questions.question: In which of the following dance forms are four aspects of abhinaya 'angika', 'aharya', 'vachika', 'satvika' and the 'nritta', 'nritya' and 'natya' combined perfectly?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama originating from the state of **Kerala, India**, and is known for its distinctive combination of dance, music, and acting.
 
• It integrates the four aspects of **abhinaya** (expression):
 
 
• **Angika** – Expression through body movements and gestures.
 
• **Aharya** – Expression through costumes, makeup, and stage props.
 
• **Vachika** – Expression through verbal communication and vocal music.
 
• **Satvika** – Expression of emotions and internal feelings.
 
 
 
• Kathakali also combines the three elements of classical dance:
 
 
• **Nritta** – Pure dance movements showcasing rhythm and technique.
 
• **Nritya** – Expressive dance movements conveying emotions and moods.
 
• **Natya** – Dramatic representation of stories through acting.
 
 
 
• The themes of Kathakali performances are often drawn from **Indian epics** like the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**, and other mythological stories.
 
• Performers wear elaborate costumes and makeup, including **brightly colored face paints** to depict various characters such as gods, demons, and humans.
 
• Musical accompaniments include traditional instruments like the **chenda** and **maddalam**, and the vocal music typically follows the Carnatic tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manipuri**__

 __
 
• **Manipuri** dance originates from the northeastern state of **Manipur, India**.
 
• It is primarily a devotional and spiritual dance form associated with **Vaishnavism** and themes from the **life of Lord Krishna**.
 
• Manipuri is known for its **graceful movements**, delicate hand gestures, and soft facial expressions.
 
• Unlike Kathakali, it does not emphasize dramatic expressions through heavy makeup or costumes.
 
• Manipuri dance is performed to the accompaniment of **classical music** and traditional instruments like the **pung** (drum) and **kartal** (cymbals).
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**__
 __
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is characterized by its precise hand gestures (**mudras**), intricate footwork, and expressions (**abhinaya**).
 
• Bharatanatyam combines **nritta, nritya, and natya**, but its focus is more on storytelling through expressive gestures rather than dramatic costumes like Kathakali.
 
• The themes of Bharatanatyam often revolve around **religious devotion**, particularly to Lord Shiva, Vishnu, and Krishna.
 
• Musical accompaniment follows the **Carnatic music tradition**.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**__
 
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It emphasizes intricate **footwork**, **spins**, and subtle facial expressions.
 
• Kathak is heavily influenced by both **Hindu mythology** and the **Mughal court** traditions.
 
• Unlike Kathakali, it does not use elaborate costumes or heavy makeup, focusing instead on the dancer's movements and expressions.
 
• Musical accompaniment includes instruments like the **tabla**, **sitar**, and **harmonium**.

questions.question: There are two identical spherical solid balls of iron alloy touching each other. What would be the gravitational force of attraction between them if the density of the materials of the ball is (3 /2π) × 105 (kg/m3) and radius 1 m. G = 6.67 × 10-11Nm2/kg2.

The Correct answer is __**0.667 N**__.

• **m₁** and **m₂** are the masses of the two spheres.

questions.question: The fluid portion of the cytosol, devoid of any cell organelles, present in both the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell is ____________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hyaloplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hyaloplasm** refers to the fluid portion of the cytosol that does not contain any cell organelles.
 
• It serves as the basic matrix or ground substance of the cytoplasm, often called the **cytoplasmic matrix**.
 
• **Hyaloplasm** is present in both **prokaryotic** and **eukaryotic cells**, serving as a medium for biochemical reactions.
 
• This fluid component is responsible for hosting various molecules, such as **enzymes, ions, and proteins**, which play crucial roles in cellular processes.
 
• It provides a structural framework for the cell and facilitates the movement of organelles and substances within the cytoplasm.
 
• The term "hyaloplasm" is derived from the Greek word "**hyalos**" meaning glass, indicating its clear and transparent nature.
 
• Unlike the organelles suspended within the cytoplasm, the hyaloplasm is devoid of any visible structures under a microscope.
 
• It plays a vital role in maintaining the **homeostasis** of the cell by balancing the distribution of ions and nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nucleoplasm**__

 __
 
• **Nucleoplasm**, also known as nuclear sap, is the fluid found inside the **nucleus** of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It serves as a medium for the suspension of nuclear components such as **chromatin** and **nucleolus**.
 
• It also plays a role in the exchange of substances between the nucleus and cytoplasm through nuclear pores.
 
 
 
• **Protoplasm**__
 __
 
• **Protoplasm** refers to the entire living content of a cell, which includes both the **cytoplasm** and **nucleoplasm**.
 
• It is considered the fundamental substance of life, hosting all vital cellular activities.
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**__
 
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes, primarily involved in **breaking down cellular waste** and recycling cellular components.
 
• They are often referred to as the **"suicide bags"** of the cell due to their role in autophagy.

questions.question: What was the primary reason for the 'Plan Holiday' between 1966 and 1969?

options.text: Failure of the Third Five-Year Plan

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Failure of the Third Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966)** in India aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in food production and increasing industrial output.
 
• However, the plan faced severe challenges due to events such as the **India-China War in 1962**, the **India-Pakistan War in 1965**, and a series of **droughts** that resulted in food shortages.
 
• The plan failed to achieve its goals, leading to substantial economic setbacks and a decline in agricultural production.
 
• Due to these challenges, the government decided to suspend further Five-Year Plans temporarily, resulting in the **'Plan Holiday'** period from 1966 to 1969.
 
• During this period, annual plans were formulated instead of long-term Five-Year Plans to focus on immediate issues such as **food production**, **economic stabilization**, and **post-war recovery**.
 
• The Plan Holiday was essential to address the economic crisis and reevaluate strategies for future planning in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Political instability**__

 __
 
• Political instability can affect economic planning, but it was not the primary reason for the Plan Holiday. The Plan Holiday was more a response to economic challenges and failures of the Third Five-Year Plan.
 
• Political instability in India during the 1960s was marked by leadership changes, such as the transition from **Jawaharlal Nehru to Lal Bahadur Shastri**, and later to **Indira Gandhi**, but this was secondary to the economic issues.
 
 
 
• **Economic liberalisation**__
 __
 
• Economic liberalisation refers to the process of reducing government restrictions on the economy, which gained prominence in India during the **1990s**, not the 1960s.
 
• It was not related to the Plan Holiday, as the focus during this time was on addressing immediate economic crises rather than liberalisation.
 
 
 
• **Deflation**__
 
 
• Deflation refers to a decrease in the general price level of goods and services. While economic issues were part of the challenges, deflation was not the direct reason for the Plan Holiday.
 
• The Plan Holiday was more focused on managing food shortages and economic instability caused by droughts and wars.
